clue.text: Tussore worked with gold for the bottom drawer (9)

indicators.note: fabric that has been worked is reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone sews silk and gold thread into linen to save for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is British for the linen and household goods a bride-to-be collects before marriage, the American hope chest; tussore is a coarse silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the bride's collection of clothes and linen, just what the bottom drawer holds.

clue.text: Exhausted Member of the Dail broken by Ireland (5)

indicators.note: TD is split open and IRE sits in the break

blocks.note: a TD (Teachta Dála) is a member of the Irish parliament
Ire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish politician is worn out by the country he serves.
explanation.walkthrough: TD is the Irish equivalent of MP: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired and exhausted both mean worn out.

clue.text: Company set up a lot of ongoing church event (10)

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up lifts the letters so they read bottom to top
most of the word, not all of it: the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A firm organises most of a parish's continuing activities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church event' looks like one phrase, but church is only CE; the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything that happens or takes place counts as both.

clue.text: Measure introduced by country, spreading from the centre (8)

indicators.note: the country takes the measure inside itself

blocks.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A nation brings in a policy that radiates outwards from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' looks like a law a country passes; it is an old unit of cloth length, about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellate means star-shaped, with points radiating from a centre.

clue.text: Order used in some dictionaries (5)

blocks.note: an electronic dictionary, e- for electronic plus the usual short form of dictionary

explanation.surface: An instruction about which reference books to consult.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: an e-dict is an electronic dictionary, so EDICT is the form some dictionaries come in.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a proclamation issued by a ruler commands obedience.

clue.text: Uncover second butterfly in centre of sand hills (9)

indicators.note: the butterfly pair goes inside
keep only the middle of the word

blocks.note: DUNES without its first and last letters; split around the insert
the heath is a family of small brown butterflies

explanation.surface: A second butterfly is spotted among the dunes, flushed out of hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: The heath butterflies, small heath and large heath, are named for the moorland they live on, which suits the sand-hill surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a blade is to draw it from its cover, so to uncover it.

clue.text: Unlit playing area has defender crossing line (5-5)

indicators.note: the defender reaches across the line, holding it inside

blocks.note: a back is a defensive player

explanation.surface: A floodlight failure on the football field while a defender steps over a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture makes 'line' a touchline; it is just L, the standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch-black means completely dark, with no light at all.

clue.text: Be very nosy about closure of stone quarry (4)

indicators.note: PRY goes round the letter
the closing letter of the word

blocks.note: to pry is to be nosy

explanation.surface: Someone snooping around the shutting down of a stone quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone quarry' reads as one place, but quarry is the definition: the hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarry is an animal being hunted, which is prey.

clue.text: Beginning to turn fish catcher’s reel (6)

indicators.note: take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An angler starts winding in the reel.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishing scene makes 'reel' a noun on a rod; it is the verb, to stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe walking unsteadily, like someone dizzy or drunk.

clue.text: One often on the job in bed? (14)

definitions.text: One often on the job in bed?

blocks.note: reads as a sexual euphemism; really someone at work
reads as the bedroom; really a flower bed

explanation.surface: A saucy hint about someone busy in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, where a gardener spends working hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A horticulturist is a gardener, who works in flower beds.

clue.text: Having abandoned property plot located round Old Street (4-3-5)

indicators.note: LAND goes round the old street

explanation.surface: A deserted property on a plot near Old Street, the London road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Located' is placed last in the answer though it sits before 'round' in the clue. A lost-and-found office holds items people have left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost-and-found office is defined by holding abandoned property.

clue.text: Crack core voice, withdrawing over and over again (7)

blocks.clueFragment: voice, withdrawing over and over again
blocks.note: VOICE with O removed, the second time

explanation.surface: A central voice drops out of the choir, time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is O in crosswords; 'over and over again' says take one O out of each of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a narrow opening or fissure in rock or a wall.

clue.text: Drive rig with energy (3-2-3-2)

blocks.note: a get-up or rig is an outfit
go = energy, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Driving a lorry, or a rig, with plenty of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'rig' pull toward trucks; drive is the noun for ambition, and a rig is a costume.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for energetic ambition, the noun sense of drive, as in someone lacking motivation.

clue.text: Hear wrongly about account — key problem for the listener? (7)

indicators.note: the letters are set down in the wrong order
the rearranged letters go round the account

blocks.note: HEAR rearranged, split to take AC

explanation.surface: Mishearing a bank statement, then asking whether the problem is a stuck key.
explanation.walkthrough: The listener is anyone with ears, and the question mark flags the play on the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain in the ear, a problem for anyone listening.

clue.text: Officer, one sometimes preceding general (9)

blocks.note: an official whose title is completed by the word 'General'

explanation.surface: An army officer who comes before a general in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The ranks picture suggests someone below a general; the wording means the word placed before 'general', as in Inspector General.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police officer, and the title Inspector General puts it before 'general'.

clue.text: Glasses with bits of dust detected (5)

indicators.note: picked up by the ear rather than seen written down

explanation.surface: Spectacles on which some dust has been noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Specks and specs are said the same way; one is the dust you see on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British shortening of spectacles, worn to correct eyesight.

clue.text: Source of radiation is up — it’s a problem for airways (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the sun radiates light and heat
it's written out in full: IT IS

explanation.surface: A radiation leak is under way, bad news for the airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airways' looks like airlines; it means the breathing passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinusitis is inflammation of the sinuses, which blocks the airways of the nose.

clue.text: Dresses too little for what they cover (12)

blocks.note: under- = too little, as in underpaid

explanation.surface: A complaint that some dresses are too skimpy for what they are meant to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb, 'dresses too little' is under-clothes; read as a noun, dresses are what cover the underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by relation: a frock is worn on top of vests, slips and knickers, hiding them.

clue.text: Thought: the settling of disputes is about time (10)

indicators.note: the settling word goes round the time

explanation.surface: A reflection that resolving arguments is mostly a matter of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes this sound like a proverb; 'Thought' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: deep, quiet contemplation of an idea is serious thinking.

clue.text: User of rack perhaps right to be fitted in large open-top car (8)

indicators.note: a part fitted in a car is installed inside it, so RT goes within TOURER

blocks.note: a tourer is a large open car

explanation.surface: Someone with a roof rack wants it fitted to a big convertible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rack' belongs on a car roof in this picture; it is the medieval torture device that stretched victims.
explanation.definitionFit: The rack was an instrument of torture, so one using it is a torturer.

clue.text: A university citation then redrafted a task for a notary (14)

indicators.note: a redrafted text is rewritten, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A university reference is rewritten, the kind of job a notary handles.
explanation.walkthrough: A notary is a lawyer who certifies documents and signatures as genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Authenticating documents, confirming they are genuine, is a notary's job.

clue.text: Name a good insect for shrew (9)

blocks.note: a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: Naming a helpful bug that feeds a small mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect picture makes shrew the small animal; it is a bad-tempered woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a scolding, overbearing woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Meeting one against Liszt, perhaps English (10)

blocks.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
Ferenc is the Hungarian first name of the composer Franz Liszt

explanation.surface: A meeting where one person objects to Liszt, possibly an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liszt, perhaps' asks for something Liszt is an example of: a man called Ferenc.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a formal gathering where people discuss business.

clue.text: Attila perhaps reportedly fears veteran divisions (8)

indicators.note: as reported by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: Attila was king of the Huns

explanation.surface: Attila, by all accounts, is afraid of battle-hardened army units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veteran divisions' pictures army units; veteran just means old, and a hundred was an old subdivision of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Hundreds were historic administrative divisions of English counties.

clue.text: Exercises with a small warning such as might get child puffing? (10)

definitions.text: such as might get child puffing?

blocks.note: a hooter is a horn or siren that sounds a warning

explanation.surface: Gym class with a gentle alert, as might leave a child out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: Puffing seems to mean breathless after exercise; the child is blowing through a tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a toy tube a child blows peas through.

clue.text: Appalling court order (6)

explanation.surface: A shocking ruling from the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court order' reads as one legal phrase; court is only CT and order is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: a boss can instruct or command staff.

clue.text: Getting into stocks for one in official garment (10)

blocks.note: a vestment is a ceremonial robe

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into medieval stocks while dressed in ceremonial robes.
explanation.walkthrough: The stocks look like the wooden punishment frame; they are shares on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying stocks and shares is one example of investment.

clue.text: Nothing once purchased loses billions (5)

indicators.note: whatever a word loses is no longer part of it, so B comes off BOUGHT

explanation.surface: Something once bought for a fortune is now worth nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an old word: ought, like aught, used to mean nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is an archaic variant of nought, meaning nothing.

clue.text: Parade of geese irregularly chased by returning doggy? (5-4)

going back, so the letters read in reverse

clue.text: Heron with tail and tibia broken gets healing treatment (14)

indicators.note: the letters are broken apart and reassembled

clue.text: Love? Halo? These in essence may appear so (4)

definitions.text: Love? Halo? These in essence may appear so

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so take the middle letters

explanation.surface: A musing on whether love and a halo look alike at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: love is 0 in tennis, and a halo is a ring, both round shapes.

clue.text: Changing environment sounded alarm for old Chinese rulers (12)

clue.text: No longer watch out after second run for free program (9)

ware! is an old warning, beware

clue.text: Young one succeeded with expedition over heather (9)
